subject: Manufacturing
summary: lathe operations and machining time, thread cutting, taper turning, drilling, shaping and planing, milling and indexing, jigs and fixtures (3-2-1 location, bushes, diamond pins), non-traditional machining (EDM relaxation circuit, ECM by Faraday's law, USM, AJM, LBM) and additive manufacturing processes and build time

questions.text: During thread cutting on a centre lathe, the carriage is moved by
opts: the feed rod through the apron gearing
engaging the split (half) nut with the lead screw, so that the carriage advances one lead per revolution of the work
hand, using the carriage hand-wheel
the cross-slide screw
questions.ans: (B) engaging the split (half) nut with the lead screw, so that the carriage advances one lead per revolution of the work
solution: Concept: A thread needs an exact, positive ratio between work rotation and tool travel.
The lead screw, driven from the spindle through change gears, moves the carriage when the half nut is closed on it: (B).
The feed rod (with friction clutches in the apron) is used for ordinary turning feeds, where slip does not matter.
Exam tip: The thread-chasing dial tells the operator when to re-engage the half nut so the tool falls into the same groove.

questions.text: A bar of 60 mm diameter is reduced to 52 mm diameter over a length of 150 mm in two passes of 2 mm depth each. The cutting speed is kept at 120 m/min, calculated on the diameter at the start of each pass. The approach is 5 mm and the feed is 0.25 mm/rev. The total machining time (in min, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: t = L/(fN) per pass, with N = 1000V/(πD) recalculated for each pass.
Total = 1.88 min
Exam tip: Each pass of depth 2 mm reduces the diameter by 4 mm.

questions.text: The essential difference between a jig and a fixture is that
opts: a fixture is used only for drilling
a jig is always heavier and is bolted to the machine table
a jig is used only on lathes
a jig holds and locates the work and also guides the cutting tool (e.g. through drill bushes), whereas a fixture only holds and locates the work
questions.ans: (D) a jig holds and locates the work and also guides the cutting tool (e.g. through drill bushes), whereas a fixture only holds and locates the work
solution: Concept: Both locate and clamp the workpiece in a fixed position.

A jig additionally guides the tool, typically with hardened bushes for drilling, reaming and tapping. A fixture is fixed to the machine table and the tool is set with setting blocks or feeler gauges, as in milling, turning and grinding: (D).
Exam tip: Drill jigs are usually not clamped to the table; milling fixtures are.

questions.text: In an RC relaxation circuit for EDM, the supply voltage is 100 V, R = 40 Ω and C = 20 μF. The discharge across the gap occurs when the capacitor voltage reaches 70 V. Neglecting the discharge time, the spark frequency (in Hz, round off to the nearest whole number) is ______
solution: Concept: The capacitor charges as Vc = Vs(1 − e−t/RC); the cycle time is the time to reach the discharge voltage.
t = RC ln[V<sub>s</sub>/(V<sub>s</sub> − V<sub>d</sub>)] = 8 × 10<sup>−4</sup> × ln(100/30) = 9.632 × 10<sup>−4</sup> s
Exam tip: The energy per spark is ½CVd2 = 0.049 J here; a higher Vd gives bigger sparks but a lower frequency.

questions.text: In electrochemical machining, the tool shows practically no wear because
opts: the tool is made of diamond
the tool is the cathode, where only hydrogen gas is evolved and no metal is dissolved
the electrolyte is a dielectric
the tool is cooled by the electrolyte
questions.ans: (B) the tool is the cathode, where only hydrogen gas is evolved and no metal is dissolved
solution: Concept: In electrolysis metal dissolves only at the anode.
The work is made the anode and dissolves; at the tool (cathode) the reaction is the release of hydrogen gas (and hydroxide ions), so the tool shape is kept: (B).
Exam tip: The electrolyte (e.g. NaCl or NaNO3 solution) is a good conductor, unlike the dielectric used in EDM.

questions.text: Aluminium (atomic weight 27, valency 3, density 2.7 g/cm³) is machined by ECM at 500 A. Taking Faraday's constant as 96 500 C/mol and 100 % efficiency, the volumetric material removal rate (in mm³/s, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Faraday's law: mass removal rate = IA/(nF).
Exam tip: The MRR does not depend on the hardness of the work, which is why ECM suits hard alloys.

questions.text: Typical operating values of tool vibration in ultrasonic machining are
opts: frequency about 20 kHz and amplitude about 15–50 μm
frequency about 50 Hz and amplitude about 1 mm
frequency about 2 MHz and amplitude about 1 nm
frequency about 20 kHz and amplitude about 5 mm
questions.ans: (A) frequency about 20 kHz and amplitude about 15–50 μm
solution: Concept: The magnetostrictive or piezoelectric transducer works just above the audible range, and a horn (concentrator) magnifies the amplitude.
Frequency ≈ 19–25 kHz and amplitude ≈ 15–50 μm: (A).
Exam tip: In Shaw's model, the MRR increases with amplitude, frequency and grain size, and is highest for brittle work materials.

questions.text: A dividing head has a 40 : 1 worm gear, and index plates with hole circles of 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20 / 21, 23, 27, 29, 31, 33 / 37, 39, 41, 43, 47, 49. To mill 52 equally spaced slots by simple indexing using the 39-hole circle, the number of holes the crank must move for each slot is ______
solution: Concept: In simple indexing, crank turns per division = 40/N.
40/52 = 10/13 (less than one turn)
10/13 = 30/39, so the crank moves 30 holes on the 39-hole circle (no full turns).
Exam tip: The sector arms are set to span 30 spaces (31 holes) so that the count cannot go wrong.

questions.text:
Match the additive manufacturing process (Column I) with its category (Column II).
P. Stereolithography (SLA)   Q. Fused deposition modelling (FDM)   R. Selective laser sintering (SLS)   S. 3D printing with a liquid binder
1. Powder bed fusion   2. Binder jetting   3. Vat photopolymerisation   4. Material extrusion
solution: Concept: ISO/ASTM 52900 groups AM processes by how each layer is made.

SLA cures liquid resin in a vat (vat photopolymerisation); FDM extrudes a molten filament (material extrusion); SLS fuses powder with a laser (powder bed fusion); binder jetting glues powder with a liquid binder: (D).
Exam tip: SLS and binder jetting need no support structures because the loose powder supports the part; SLA and FDM need supports for overhangs.

questions.text: A part 36 mm high is built by stereolithography with a layer thickness of 0.1 mm. Each layer takes 20 s for laser scanning and 10 s for recoating. The build time (in min) is ______
solution: Concept: Build time = number of layers × time per layer.
Exam tip: Halving the layer thickness improves the surface (smaller stair steps) but doubles the number of layers and so roughly doubles the build time.

questions.text: Abrasive jet machining is NOT well suited for
opts: cutting thin sections of glass
deburring and frosting of hard brittle parts
machining soft, ductile materials such as lead or soft aluminium, where the abrasive embeds in the surface
drilling small holes in ceramics
questions.ans: (C) machining soft, ductile materials such as lead or soft aluminium, where the abrasive embeds in the surface
solution: Concept: In AJM a high-velocity stream of fine abrasive in a gas jet erodes the work by brittle fracture.
Ductile materials deform instead of chipping, and the grains tend to embed in soft surfaces, so the MRR is very low: (C).
Exam tip: Typical abrasives are Al2O3 and SiC of 10–50 μm, at gas pressures of a few bar and jet velocities of 150–300 m/s.

questions.text: A surface 250 mm long is slab milled with a cutter of 80 mm diameter and 6 teeth at 200 rpm, with a feed of 0.15 mm per tooth and a depth of cut of 5 mm, as shown. Taking the approach as √(d(D − d)) and neglecting over-travel, the machining time (in min, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: The cutter reaches full depth only after its centre has moved the approach A = √(d(D − d)) from the point of first contact.
Table feed = f<sub>z</sub>zN = 0.15 × 6 × 200 = 180 mm/min
Exam tip: In face milling with the cutter central, the approach is D/2 instead.

questions.text: In a planing machine, as distinct from a shaper,
opts: the work, mounted on the table, reciprocates under a stationary tool, and the tool is fed between strokes
the tool reciprocates and the work is fed
the work rotates and the tool is fed axially
the tool rotates and the work is fed
questions.ans: (A) the work, mounted on the table, reciprocates under a stationary tool, and the tool is fed between strokes
solution: Concept: Both produce flat surfaces with single-point tools in straight strokes.
In a shaper the ram carries the tool over a stationary work; in a planer the heavy table carries the large work past the tool: (A).
Exam tip: Planers are used for large, heavy jobs (machine beds); shapers for small jobs.

questions.text: A hole of 0.4 mm diameter is to be drilled through a 1.5 mm thick steel sheet by a pulsed laser. Each pulse has an energy of 2 J, of which 40 % is absorbed, and the energy needed to vaporise steel is 60 J/mm³. The minimum number of pulses needed is ______
solution: Concept: Pulses needed = energy to remove the hole volume/absorbed energy per pulse (rounded up).
Energy = 0.1885 × 60 = 11.31 J; absorbed per pulse = 0.4 × 2 = 0.8 J
Pulses = 11.31/0.8 = 14.14, so 15 pulses
Exam tip: Always round up the number of pulses (or passes); 14 pulses would leave the hole incomplete.

questions.text: In the 3-2-1 principle of location for a prismatic workpiece,
opts: three clamps, two locators and one support are used
the work is held by three jaws, two centres and one stop
only three locators are needed for complete location
six locators are used: three on the primary (base) plane, two on the secondary plane and one on the tertiary plane, which together with the clamps restrain all 12 degrees of freedom
questions.ans: (D) six locators are used: three on the primary (base) plane, two on the secondary plane and one on the tertiary plane, which together with the clamps restrain all 12 degrees of freedom
solution: Concept: A free body has 12 degrees of freedom (±translation and ±rotation about three axes).

Three points on the base restrain 5 (−Z and rotations about X and Y, both senses), two on a side face restrain 3 more (−X and both senses of rotation about Z), and one on the end face restrains 1 more (−Y): 9 by the 6 locators.
The clamps restrain the remaining 3 (+X, +Y, +Z): (D).
Exam tip: The three base locators should be spread as widely as possible for a stable seating.
